messages:
alice: Saw a customer report where the console shows metrics from the previous org after quick switching. Screenshot attached in thread.
ben: Ugh. Repro steps? browser, account, quick switch timing?
ale: Happens during fast org-switch (click org nav -> pick org B) then open Dashboard > Insights iframe.
carol: I saw something similar last week in staging. iframe caches query results and we were missing the workspace scope header in some proxy code.
dinesh: Can you paste request/response headers from the failing trace? suspect X-Workspace-ID vs jwt.org claim mismatch.
alice: Attaching a sanitized trace:

Request: GET /api/insights?panel=usage  HTTP/1.1
Host: console.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
X-Workspace-ID: w-890
Cookie: session=eyJhbGci...

Response payload (partial): {"data": {"events": [...org: w-123 ...]}}

ben: That response payload indicates the service returned w-123 results while header was w-890. Means either cache key or context derivation bug.
carol: The embeddable proxy (insights-proxy) has this in middleware:
```js
ctx.workspace = req.headers['x-workspace-id'] || jwt.claims.workspace
cacheKey = `insights:${ctx.workspace}:${panel}:${range}`
```
If req.headers present but invalid, we still use it. We had a rollout that prefers header for quicker local debugging (rbac-filtering-v2).
dinesh: On top of that, redis namespace setup uses `workspace.slice(0,8)` in one place (old perf hack). Collision possible between w-12345abc and w-12345def truncated -> w-12345ab.
elaine: Oof. We rolled that feature to 20% yesterday for hosted and 100% for dedicated. Could explain why only some orgs reported it.
ben: Quick mitigation: 1) stop honoring X-Workspace-ID from untrusted sources 2) clear affected redis keys 3) add short-term signal in telemetry for cross-tenant payloads.
dinesh: I'll own the hotfix PR: verify workspace derives from jwt.claims.org_id first, then fall back to header only if header == jwt.claims.org_id. Also remove any truncation in cache key code path.
carol: I'll create an integration test that exercises fast org switch + iframe rehydrate. Will add a flaky-tolerance harness to catch race.
infra-bot: deploy: prod cluster had a new deploy 2026-03-12T18:22:10Z sha=0a1b2c3 (rbac-filtering-v2 rollout)
deploy-bot: rolling back job queued for 0a1b2c3? (manual)
elaine: Can we also add a one-off job to scan logs for responses where payload.org != jwt.claims.org_id and alert? we need to know impact.
ben: Agree. Add metric `cross_tenant_query.count` and include sample request id (scrubbed).
dinesh: PR opened -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/5123 (hotfix + cache key change). Will push to staging in ~30m.
carol: Tested locally against the repro and staging; iframe no longer pulls old org data after switch.
alice: Thanks. I'll ping customer and ask them to verify after fix.
elaine: Follow-ups: retro to cover rollout gating & canary coverage, add e2e for org-switches, and update runbook for cache clears.
ben: Note: quota service also uses `org_id || workspace_id` ordering in one route. We should audit similar codepaths (billing, quotas, telemetry).
dinesh: Adding TODOs to PR description. Will include migration script to rename any truncated keys and a small script to emit backfill counts.
carol: :eyes: :fire:
alice: Customer pinged, they confirmed lower impact but showed it twice. Will update once they validate fix.
ben: Nice catch. Good fallback plan.
deploy-bot: rollback executed for sha=0a1b2c3 at 1851234608
infra-bot: prod: hotfix deploy scheduled 1851234612 sha=0f9e8d7
carol: Will run integration runbook against prod hotfix after deploy.
dinesh: Marking issue for postmortem. I'll draft initial timeline.
